name: Background location
plain: Lets the app read location when it is closed or not on screen.
meaning: Builds a continuous movement history: home, work, visits, trips. The strongest location grant, and the one platforms push users to avoid.

android.permission: ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION; foreground services need type location
android.prompt_ui: Android 11+: no in-app dialog; app sends the user to Settings to choose Allow all the time
android.persistence: Until revoked; auto-reset after months unused
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Permissions > Location > Allow all the time
android.store_policy: Play: declaration form plus review; must be core to the app (policy since 2020, enforced 2021)
android.note: Android 10 had a dialog; Android 11 moved it to Settings. Foreground-service location needs user to have granted foreground access first.

ios.prompt_ui: Always prompt is deferred (iOS 13+): app asks While Using first, then iOS shows Keep While Using or Change to Always later
ios.persistence: Until revoked; iOS shows periodic reminders (map of recorded locations)
ios.store_policy: App Review 2.5.4 and 5.1.1: background location only for features that need it
ios.note: Blue pill or arrow appears while a background session is active; significant change monitoring wakes a terminated app.

data.metric: Location fixes while the app is not visible
data.update: Android: a few per hour in background (API 26+ throttling); iOS: significant change about 500 m, or continuous

limits.headline: Can follow your location when the app is closed, after you choose Always allow
limits.user_action: You tap Always Allow, or choose Allow all the time in Settings
can: Keep your location updates running with the app closed
Alert you when you enter or leave a place (geofence)
Wake the app on a big move, even if it was ended, on iPhone
Show a blue pill or arrow on iPhone while it runs
cannot: Run in the background without a second step on Android 11 and newer, where Settings holds the setting
Hide that it is tracking; iPhone shows an indicator and Android shows a notice for foreground services
Use background location before you grant foreground location
Keep going after you pick While using the app or turn it off
limits.differs: Android 11 and newer sends you to Settings for the second step. iPhone asks, then reminds you from time to time.

story.what_it_is: An app can read your location even when it is closed or not on the screen.

marketing.name: Background location
marketing.pitch: Android needs a separate step and a clear reason before apps can use location in the background.

marketing.name: Always location
marketing.pitch: Apple asks you to choose Always, While Using the App, or Never so you control background access.

story.for_you: You see a prompt that says Always or Allow all the time. If you agree, the app can follow you all day, and you may see a blue bar or arrow on the status bar. It keeps working even when you forget about it.
story.for_makers: Makers need it for tasks that must work when you are not looking: trip tracking, geofence alerts and sharing location with family. It also creates a full movement history, and the data can be sold. Platforms push users to avoid this setting.

use_cases.example: A run tracker keeps recording your route when your phone is in your pocket and the screen is off.
A family app shows where each person is in near real time and alerts you when they arrive home.
A driver app keeps sharing the car's location between trips so riders see it move.
An AR game keeps counting distance and spawns things when you walk with the app closed.
A delivery app lets a customer watch a courier come closer even when the courier's phone is locked.
A hidden software kit logs your movements all day and sells them to data brokers.

story.android_note: Android 10 and later need a separate Allow all the time step, and Play requires a stated reason and review.
story.ios_note: iPhone asks for While Using first, then later offers Always, and shows a blue indicator when an app uses it.

technical_bounds: Apps cannot jump straight to Always on either platform
Visible indicator on iOS; Android shows a foreground notification for foreground services

abuse: Silent movement logs sold to brokers

history.change: ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION split out of foreground location
No in-app dialog; users must grant All the time in Settings
Background location updates throttled to a few per hour
Always becomes a deferred second prompt with a map reminder
